profile.name: Pranav Ray
profile.title: Systems & Distributed Backend
profile.bio: building concurrent architectures, peer-to-peer networks, and zero-dependency low-level engines in Go.
profile.aboutFull: basically, i just like building backend systems. a lot. nowadays i'm designing concurrent architectures thus diving deep into peer-to-peer networks and distributed systems. in my free time, i like to write blogs, read, solve algorithms and pretend to be good at chess.

projects.title: tunneru
projects.description: a lightweight zero-dependency tunneling engine, binary multiplexer, and real-time request inspection suite built in raw go from first principles. features custom 9-byte binary stream framing, interactive bubble tea terminal tui telemetry, and a next.js web dashboard with 1-click webhook replay.
projects.longDescription: tunneru is a lightweight zero-dependency tunneling engine, binary multiplexer, and real-time request inspection suite built in raw go from first principles without using external tunneling services or third-party cloud lock-in. it implements custom stream multiplexing over a single persistent tcp connection using an ultra-compact 9-byte binary frame header with zero-allocation fast-path parsing and sub-millisecond dispatch latency. tunneru provides dual telemetry: an interactive terminal tui built with bubble tea and lipgloss for live request streaming, and a dedicated next.js web dashboard with json tree inspection, raw header diffs, and 1-click webhook replay. it supports instant public subdomain routing and shared token authentication.

projects.title: hotaru
projects.description: p2p mesh network & distributed file dispersal system written in raw go. breaks files into chunks, scatters them encrypted across nodes, and reconstructs on demand.
projects.longDescription: hotaru is a decentralized peer-to-peer network and distributed storage system built from first principles in Go without libp2p or external frameworks. Nodes form a self-organizing mesh topology using custom TCP framing, automated peer discovery via UDP broadcasts, and dynamic routing tables. Files are sharded into deterministic chunks, hashed using BLAKE3, encrypted via AES-256-GCM, and dispersed redundantly across available network peers. Features real-time SSE streaming to a Next.js visualization dashboard tracking cluster topology and transfer telemetry.

projects.title: tsuna
projects.description: udp hole punching & direct peer-to-peer packet streaming engine in golang. bypasses symmetrical and cone nat gateways without relay servers.
projects.longDescription: tsuna demonstrates how to achieve direct UDP hole punching across complex NAT architectures without relying on third-party TURN relay proxies. Includes a lightweight coordination rendezvous server and client daemon that negotiate public endpoint mappings, punch bidirectional NAT pinholes, and establish low-latency peer-to-peer channels for direct socket transmission. Features an interactive terminal UI built with Bubbletea and Cobra.

projects.title: typingterminal
projects.description: real-time multiplayer typing speed combat and leaderboard engine built with convex and next.js.
projects.longDescription: terminaltype is a competitive typing platform featuring sub-10ms real-time state synchronization, live spectator rooms, dynamic WPM calculation, and concurrent keystroke verification powered by Convex server functions. Built with responsive dark mode aesthetics and fluid keyboard ergonomics.

projects.longDescription: tobira provides transparent reverse proxying, TLS termination, path-based routing, and real-time HTTP metrics. Implemented with concurrent worker pools in Go, streaming WebSocket telemetry to an interactive web inspector for live debugging.
